glm.feedback:
## Findings

**1. Category: bug — Severity: high**
File: `client/src/hooks/useTerminalExpanded.ts` (the `useCallback(() => set(!expanded), [])` line)
Finding: `toggle` is memoized with an empty dependency array, so it closes over the module-level `expanded` value captured at first render (`false`). Every call to `toggle` therefore calls `set(true)` — the control can expand but never collapse. The rewrite to a module store dropped the `setState(v => !v)` updater pattern without replacing it.
Suggestion: Drop the `useCallback` (or depend on `value`), or make `set` accept an updater: `set((v) => !v)`. Note that both the new unit test ("two consumers share one state… toggles back to false") and the V8 e2e (`expand.click(); expect … not.toHaveAttribute("data-term-expanded")`) will fail with this code as written — the change cannot be green as shipped, so this is not just latent.

**2. Category: bug — Severity: medium**
File: `client/src/components/external/mission/MissionInfoSidebar.tsx` — `closeTab`
Finding: `closeTab` reads `tabs`/`target` from the render closure. It is invoked from `ViewerTabBar.onClose`, which is fine for single clicks, but the embed card and the Mission card can both be mounted simultaneously; more importantly, if two closes are dispatched in the same tick (e.g. "close others"/rapid clicks) the second close operates on stale `tabs` and can resurrect or keep a closed tab. Lower risk than #1 but the previous page-level `handleCloseTab` used functional updates.
Suggestion: Use functional updates: `setTabs(prev => …)` and derive the fallback target inside the updater (or via an effect on `tabs`/`target` mismatch).

**3. Category: regression — Severity: medium**
File: `client/src/components/external/FolderTree.tsx` — removal of the `flat` prop
Finding: The `flat` prop was deleted outright rather than deprecated. All in-repo callers shown are updated, but any external/undisplayed consumer passing `flat` now gets `undefined` and silently loses the card chrome distinction — no error, just a visual regression. Same for the default class changing from `ft-card ft-files` to `ft-flat` for every caller that did not opt into `headBand`.
Suggestion: Verify by grep that no other call sites pass `flat` (including storybook/examples); if any exist, keep a temporary alias or fail loudly.

**4. Category: edge-case — Severity: low**
File: `client/src/components/external/mission/MissionInfoSidebar.tsx` — embed + `unassigned` task
Finding: For an unassigned task on the Files & Terminal card, `EMBED_OPTIONS` is used regardless — that's correct (no Folders anyway) — but `openTarget` from `MissionInfoPanel.onOpenOutput` produces `{outside: true}` targets that get added as tabs whose `path` may collide with a project-relative tab of the same path string; `addTab` dedupes by `path` only, so opening the session output for a path already open as a project tab silently switches meaning of the tab (session vs project view) depending on which `target` object survives in `tabs`.
Suggestion: Key tabs on `path + outside` (or disambiguate in the tab label), not `path` alone.

**5. Category: test — Severity: low**
File: `client/e2e/flows/V8-files-terminal-shared-ui.spec.ts` — head-band geometry check
Finding: The 46px assertion only checks each head's height and the left-vs-right y-alignment (`boxes[0]` vs `boxes[2]`); the middle head (`boxes[1]`) is never checked to be in the same band, so a vertically offset terminal head would still pass.
Suggestion: Assert all three `y` values are within 2px of each other.

## Overall assessment

The architecture matches the spec well (shared tree, shared Info|Viewer sidebar in the single 46px head band, phone single tab bar, pty untouched), and test coverage is unusually thorough. However, finding #1 is a hard functional bug — the Expand control cannot be un-toggled — and the included tests prove it, so this cannot be green as-is.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
